newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bond mkt too bearish on economy-govt source.
newsitem.headline: Japan bond mkt too bearish on economy-govt source.

text.p: The Japanese government bond market is a bit too pessimistic about the outlook for the economy, a government source told Reuters on Tuesday.

Referring to the falling yields of Japanese government bonds, the source said: "The market is a bit too pessimistic about the outlook for the economy. It's not a situation that the downside risk for the economy is on the horizon," he said.
The source added: "Ruling out the possibility of an interest rate rise within this year is a bit premature."
Recent economic data has shown a mixed picture for current economic activity and future prospects.
"The economy may be levelling off but has not shown signs of falling back. Therefore, the economic situation does not guarantee a steady fall in long-term interest rates," he added.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond hit a record low of 2.070 percent on Monday. It was standing at 2.075 percent at 0546 GMT.
The government source said the negative effects of the sales tax increase in April were seen in such areas as car sales and department store sales.
But it is unlikely car makers will cut back their production due to booming exports.
"For every bright economic statistic released, there are three weak ones released," he added.

Asked about Monday's reported comments by Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso about a possible rise in interest rates by the end of this year, the source said there were no discussions among government bodies about interest rates for now. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-1396
